source: CNBC Squawk on the Street — Jensen Huang statement, Baker/Gerstner letter urging slow Nvidia CEO process, AI cycle not peaking in 2026, export controls vs Huawei ecosystem
summary: Jensen Huang is an irreplaceable CEO and NVDA's competitive moat is substantially tied to his personal relationships and vision
summary_extended: Baker argues that Jensen Huang is an irreplaceable, once-in-a-generation CEO whom he ranks as 'N of 2' alongside Elon Musk, and that Nvidia's competitive moat is substantially tied to Jensen's personal vision and decades-long supply chain relationships in Taiwan — relationships so deep that buildings and highways in Taipei were lit up in his honor. Baker, who has known Jensen for roughly 30 years, states unequivocally that 'there is no one' who could replace him, and that he co-signed a letter with Gerstner urging Nvidia's board to conduct a slow, deliberate CEO succession process. The investment implication is that Nvidia's long-term competitive position is materially at risk without Jensen, and Baker points to the stock's negative move following news of his potential departure as the market's own verdict on this thesis. Baker frames continued Nvidia shareholding as contingent on Jensen's leadership, making this a key single-person-dependency risk for long-term NVDA investors.
detail: Baker argues Jensen is 'N of 2' alongside Elon Musk as exceptional CEOs. His supply chain relationships in Taiwan (buildings and highways lit up in Taipei) represent a real competitive advantage that cannot easily be replicated. Baker implies NVDA's long-term competitive position is at risk without Jensen, and the stock move since his departure reflects the market's verdict.
